newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gives king-sized welcome to Spanish royals.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gives king-sized welcome to Spanish royals.

text.p: Cannons roared and the main streets were festooned with Spanish and Mexican flags as Mexico on Friday greeted King Juan Carlos and Queen Sofia of Spain.
Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo led the king and queen through a ceremony at the beautifully manicured polo grounds belonging to the Mexican army.

Hundreds of honour guards lined up like so many toy soldiers as the king, who is Spain's head of state, and Zedillo spoke of the importance of the official visit, in which the king will preside over a conference on the Spanish language next week in the north-central city of Zacatecas.
The conference "will mark the start of several meetings to fully analyse the situation of Spanish in the media in all of its current and diverse forms," Juan Carlos said.
Spanish is the primary language for 21 countries.
"This is a special theme of interest in these times with the phenomenon of globalization influencing the language in such a decisive way," he said.

The king, who also will meet with Mexican business leaders, noted that this year marks the 20th anniversary of the re-establishment of diplomatic ties between the two countries, severed during the rule of Spanish Gen. Francisco Franco.
Mexico and Spain share a long and complex history dating to the brutal Spanish conquest of Mexico, then called New Spain, in the 16th century.

Many Mexicans to this day are still coming to terms with their dual Spanish-Indian identity, often referred to in both popular culture and intellectual circles as that of a child whose father raped his mother.

But the king, who arrived with the queen on Thursday night, and the president spoke of warm and cordial relations between the two governments and peoples that exist today. "This visit comes from great friends who respect and love Mexico," Zedillo said, "from sincere friends who know and appreciate our history and our culture."
